open_points.subject: `bindings` dependency graph
open_points.text:
This list says which modules' knowledge `bindings` may rely on; it declares no
dependency edge and no imported symbol. Its edges and the exact symbols on
each are its `imports.module_internal` (SPEC_STANDARD §7), the one
authoritative source.
open_points.question: What are the required dependency directions and minimal imported symbols between `bindings` and each of `models`, `data_provider`, `canonical_values`, `clock`, `store`, `installation` and `service_invoker`, and which knowledge is instead passed into `bindings` by callers?
options: `bindings` has a direct edge to every listed module and imports the minimal symbols it uses
Only modules whose symbols `bindings` directly names have edges; all other listed knowledge is supplied through arguments
Some listed providers depend on `bindings` and invoke its capabilities, so the runtime direction is the reverse
An orchestration module obtains the listed knowledge and calls both `bindings` and the providers, leaving no direct edge
open_points.default_guess: Declare only minimal direct imports actually named by `bindings`; have `service_invoker` depend on `bindings.check_binding_current` for the mandatory pre-send stale check, and pass request-shape facts into `bindings` without a reverse runtime edge.

open_points.subject: `flows` dependency graph
open_points.text:
This list says which modules' knowledge `flows` may rely on; it declares no
dependency edge and no imported symbol. Its edges and the exact symbols on
each are its `imports.module_internal` (SPEC_STANDARD §7), the one
authoritative source.
open_points.question: What are the required dependency directions and minimal imported symbols between `flows` and each of `models`, `data_provider`, `canonical_values`, `clock`, `store`, `functions` and `bindings`, particularly for reading current contract versions, binding status and declared classes during proof and activation?
options: `flows` directly imports query capabilities from `functions` and `bindings` and the minimal symbols it uses from the other listed modules
A caller supplies contract versions and binding facts to `flows`, so `flows` has no runtime edges to `functions` or `bindings`
`flows` reads all required records directly from `store`, making `functions` and `bindings` knowledge-only references
`functions` and `bindings` call into `flows` when their records change, reversing one or both dependency directions
open_points.default_guess: Give `flows` minimal direct read dependencies on the authoritative `functions` and `bindings` capabilities, plus only the model, store, clock, canonical-value and data-provider symbols its implementation names.
